subject.title: [Feature]: Let Apple Watch connect as a direct Gateway node

question: Should Apple Watch become an opt-in direct Gateway node with its own device-scoped credential and bounded foreground-only capability set, or should the watch remain iPhone-relay-only for now?
rationale: This crosses product UX, watchOS networking, Gateway auth, node capability whitelisting, and credential storage boundaries, so automation should not choose the permanent contract.

options.title: Approve scoped direct-node design
options.body: Implement the direct mode as a separate, opt-in watch credential with secure reachable Gateway URL, foreground-only session, bounded commands, and relay fallback unchanged.

options.title: Keep relay-only for now
options.body: Defer direct watch networking until maintainers want to own the hardware proof, security posture, and support burden.

options.title: Split design first
options.body: Track setup handoff, watch credential storage, Gateway node capability whitelist, and Canvas browser handoff as separate design tasks before implementation.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped direct-node design
recommendation.body: Implement the direct mode as a separate, opt-in watch credential with secure reachable Gateway URL, foreground-only session, bounded commands, and relay fallback unchanged.
